newsitem.title: ITALY: Food summit security upped after "Gene bean" streak.
newsitem.headline: Food summit security upped after "Gene bean" streak.

text.p: A U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit reconvened on Thursday amid tighter security after three women caught police on the hop and stripped naked in front of U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman.

The summit streak on Wednesday at Glickman's news conference in the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) headquarters embarrassed Italian security chiefs who have some 10,000 police on the beat to guard some 80 of the world's leaders.
Police enforced extra checks on journalists entering the Fascist-era building on Thursday, searching bags and demanding identity documents in addition to summit accreditation tags.
"We have to do this. It's because of what happened yesterday," one police officer at the summit told a reporter.
Wednesday's demonstration was staged by protesters opposed to genetic manipulation of U.S. soybeans.

The three women, who had painted "The Naked Truth" on their bodies, and clothed supporters who held up a banner reading "Ban The Gene Bean", had media accreditation for the five-day summit, FAO sources said.
They had a free hand at the news conference for several minutes before Italian Carabinieri paramilitary police finally arrived to escort them off the premises.
Summit sources said a mix-up over security meant that no American secret servicemen were in the building with Glickman and the U.S. delegation.
Several delegations have brought their own bodyguards to Rome, including Azerbaijan which has now fewer than 11 security officers, according to an FAO list.

The summit, which opened on Wednesday with passage of a plan to halve world hunger in 20 years, was continuing with speeches from dozens of delegates, including ministers from Zaire, Libya, Russia and North Korea.
